RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Morgan Foster
Member ID: W162894592
Reference Number: POC-F4C641ED8B-99591
Date of Notice: 2026-08-23
Requested Service: Lower back disc surgery/decompression, CPT 63030
Appeal Deadline: 2027-02-19 (within 180 days of notice date)

To the Appeals and Grievances Department:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 63030 (posterior extradural laminotomy/laminectomy for exploration/decompression of neural elements or excision of herniated intervertebral disk), as stated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-23. The stated reason for denial was that "the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity."

The applicable Ambetter/Centene clinical policy governing this procedure is:

Clinical Policy: Disc Decompression Procedures
Reference Number: CP.MP.114
Date of Last Revision: 04/25
URL: https://www.ambetterhealth.com/content/dam/centene/ambetteril/clinical-policies/CP.MP.114.pdf

This policy states, in relevant part:

"It is the policy of health plans affiliated with Centene Corporation® that open discectomy and microdiscectomy are medically necessary when meeting all of the following: A. Age ≥ 18 years; B. Diagnosis of herniated lumbar disc; C. Nerve root compression confirmed by imaging and one of the following: ... 2. Radiculopathy with sensory deficit as evidenced by pain, parasthesias or numbness in a nerve root distribution, and member/enrollee has failed to respond to conservative therapy including all the following: a. ≥ four weeks physical therapy or prescribed home exercise program, or documentation of member/enrollee's inability to tolerate; b. ≥ four weeks activity modification; c. One of the following: i. NSAID or acetaminophen ≥ three weeks unless contraindicated or not tolerated; ii. Epidural steroid injection."

The clinical record submitted with the prior authorization request demonstrates that each of these elements is met:

1. Age ≥ 18 years: [confirm patient date of birth/age not stated in the records provided; to be supplied].

2. Diagnosis of herniated lumbar disc: MRI of the lumbar spine dated 2026-06-26 documents an "L4-L5 disc extrusion."

3. Nerve root compression confirmed by imaging: The same MRI documents "severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root."

4. Radiculopathy with sensory deficit, evidenced by pain, paresthesias, or numbness in a nerve root distribution: The clinical summary documents 24 months of progressive low back pain with radicular pain radiating into the right calf, positive provocative testing on the affected side, and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged L4-L5 level.

5. Failed conservative therapy, including all required components:
   a. ≥ four weeks physical therapy or home exercise program: The patient completed 12 weeks (18 visits) of supervised physical therapy, including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility work, from 2026-04-24 to 2026-07-17, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note. This exceeds the ≥ four-week requirement.
   b. ≥ four weeks activity modification: [The clinical summary does not explicitly document a period of activity modification separate from physical therapy; the patient's inability to stand more than 10 minutes reflects a significant functional limitation, but documentation specifically labeled "activity modification" should be obtained from the treating provider and submitted with this appeal if available.]
   c. NSAID/acetaminophen ≥ three weeks, or epidural steroid injection: The patient used NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief, exceeding the ≥ three-week requirement. In addition, the patient received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-17 with only 4 weeks of partial relief. [The records provided do not specify whether this injection was administered via the epidural route; if it was an epidural steroid injection, this independently satisfies criterion C.2.c.ii and should be confirmed by the treating provider's procedure note.]

I note that Section I of CP.MP.114 identifies open discectomy and microdiscectomy — the category of procedure described by CPT 63030 — as the medically necessary standard of care when the above criteria are met. Section II of the same policy, which discusses minimally invasive procedures that "have not been proven superior to other existing technologies," does not apply to the requested service, as CPT 63030 is not among the listed minimally invasive or percutaneous techniques.

Based on the documentation summarized above — a 24-month history of progressive, function-limiting low back and radicular pain; MRI-confirmed L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and L5 nerve root compression; a positive neurologic examination; and a fully documented trial of conservative therapy including 12 weeks of supervised physical therapy, 6 months of NSAID use, and a corticosteroid injection — the requested surgery meets the medical necessity criteria set forth in CP.MP.114. I respectfully request that the plan reverse its denial and approve CPT 63030 as requested by Dr. Reyes.

Enclosed with this appeal are the following records referenced above:
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-04-24 to 2026-07-17, 18 visits)
- Lumbar spine MRI report dated 2026-06-26
- Documentation of NSAID trial and corticosteroid injection dated 2026-06-17
- Clinic notes documenting functional limitations and neurologic examination findings
- [Letter of medical necessity from Dr. Reyes, if not already on file]
- [Additional documentation of activity modification and injection route, if available]

Please note that this appeal is being submitted within the 180-day deadline stated in the denial notice (by 2027-02-19).

I ask that this appeal, along with all enclosed clinical documentation, be reviewed against the plan's own medical necessity criteria in CP.MP.114. Please send written confirmation of receipt of this appeal and notify me and Dr. Reyes of the outcome and any further steps required.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter. Please contact me at [phone] or [email] if additional information is needed.

Sincerely,

Morgan Foster
Member ID: W162894592

cc: [Dr. Reyes, orthopedic surgery — office contact information]

---
Note to patient: The quoted policy language above was retrieved directly from Ambetter Illinois' publicly posted Clinical Policy CP.MP.114, "Disc Decompression Procedures." Bracketed items indicate information not present in the clinical summary provided; these should be confirmed with your provider's office before this letter is submitted. No policy language beyond what is quoted above has been paraphrased as if it were the plan's own wording — all other analysis in this letter reflects only comparison of your records to the plan's stated criteria.
